status: CPU-only browser paired comparison of partial hit-target move elision, including drag/release planning guards.
command: CHROME_BIN='/Applications/Google Chrome.app/Contents/MacOS/Google Chrome' WASM_BINDGEN_TEST_RUNNER=<wasm-bindgen-test-runner 0.2.127> ROUTING_BROWSER_TIMEOUT_SECONDS=45 node scripts/measure_node_graph_browser.mjs <variant.wasm>
method: Each run launches fresh isolated headless Chrome, executes both CPU benchmark tests, and preserves twenty warm samples per size and twenty pointer-driven release/idle cycles. No concurrent Cargo work during sampling; immutable copied wasm artifacts per variant. Final trial schedule chosen before execution: randomized baseline/candidate order within each of three pairs. No application composition, GPU execution/upload, or presentation measurement. Median of per-run medians/p95s and ranges are descriptive, not confidence intervals. Preliminary variants and their reports are retained separately and are not pooled into final summaries. Final summaries refer only to candidate-v4 trials; earlier v3 reports remain separate. Whole-frame identity equality guards cover deleted targets left registered during the same pass.

candidate-v1.description: Retained native prototype plus eligibility regression; move plan built even during fast dragging.

candidate-v2.description: Skip move planning during fast rendering, but still plan on canvas-only allocation release frames.

candidate-v3.description: Plan only when initial node targets were allocated and current rendering is not fast. Other eligibility rules unchanged.

candidate-v4.description: Plan only after initial node-target allocation and outside fast rendering. Full raising on any change to overall node/header/toggle/socket target identities or minimap visibility; per-node geometry and isolation guards unchanged.
